0.long_answer: Mandibular prognathism, where the lower jaw is excessively protruding so that the lower teeth are positioned ahead of the upper teeth, is typically associated with a Class III malocclusion. In Angle's classification of malocclusion, Class III describes a scenario in which the lower incisor edges lie anterior to the cingulum plateau of the upper incisors, often resulting in an underbite. This condition may occur due to skeletal discrepancies, such as an overgrown mandible or a short maxilla, leading to an imbalance in the relationship between the dental arches.
